blocks.fleet-v1:
Host safety (fleet-v1):
- This block is the single test and host rule for a fleet session. Where a repository's AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or README says otherwise about tests, that text is for people and CI; follow this block.
- Tests: run only tests for what you changed locally; leave full suites to CI. Database integration tests belong in CI: do not start local database servers, even where a repo file shows how.
- Test host: every host, mbp-server included, follows the same rule (operator decision 237, hk 4496): run `go test` for the packages you changed directly in your worktree; full suites (`go test ./...`), `-race` sweeps and database tests stay with the PR's CI.
- Stop every fixture or background process you start, by its PID, before finishing.
- Work only in a worktree, never in the canonical checkout: other sessions share that checkout.
- Reporting upward (READY, ESC, other notices): use only `panewire emit --kind lane.event --lane <parent-lane> --type <ready|decision|blocked|info>`, whatever harness the parent runs; an ESC is `--type decision`, being stuck is `--type blocked`. Never write into the parent pane with herdr prompt/send-text/send-keys: the text lands in that pane's input box. emit rc 0 is enough even when you cannot see the receiver, so do not raise an ESC about delivery.
- Completion: a report file alone never completes a job. READY or DONE in a lane.event from this pane completes the job once the report exists and has stopped changing; an optional `[label] ` prefix is allowed. `panewire done` completes directly. `panewire escalate` stops with a reason. ESC asks a question and keeps the job open.
- Finishing work: keep going until the brief's Done section (or, without one, its stated deliverable) is met. Do not end a turn with a list of what remains, an offer to continue, or a wait that nothing will wake. Difficulty or size is never a reason to stop; neither is elapsed time.
- Ordinary obstacles are yours to work through: an error, a timeout, a busy or failing tool, an empty result, a flaky test. Diagnose, then wait and retry, fix the request, or use another tool. These steps need no approval: re-reading a file or record, repeating a read-only command, re-running a failed test or build, `git merge origin/<base>` on your own branch, and a bounded wait for a signal you named.
- Deliberate blockers are left alone: a credential you do not hold through a tool, an operator-only action, another lane's worktree, a rule in this preamble. Say what you found in an ESC and carry on with the parts of the brief that do not depend on the answer.
